body_markdown:
The calendar may say it’s fall, but on Spotify, the holiday season has begun. This year, we’re getting into the spirit early with Holidays on Spotify, a season-long celebration packed with surprise data drops, new releases, and plenty of festive moments to soundtrack the months ahead.


If you’ve had the itch for a wintry jingle lately, you aren’t alone. Holiday listening has already begun in earnest on Spotify: We’re seeing festive favorites being streamed 36.2 million times a day on average, with “


[Merry Christmas, Please Don’t Call](https://open.spotify.com/track/0UOG0zUn7t8m8QcxfzR7AH?si=d6066fd78f134ad3) ” by


[Bleachers](https://open.spotify.com/artist/2eam0iDomRHGBypaDQLwWI) currently the most-popular holiday-themed track of the year, followed by


“


[Merry Christmas, i miss you](https://open.spotify.com/track/0XYALktGbnHJ1TdW0Oz5KN?autoplay_ok=1) ” by


**[Alex Crichton](https://open.spotify.com/artist/25JtC3l1STnE2GptoHKXdD)** , “


[Snowman](https://open.spotify.com/track/7uoFMmxln0GPXQ0AcCBXRq) ” by


**[Sia](https://open.spotify.com/artist/5WUlDfRSoLAfcVSX1WnrxN)** , “


[Last Christmas](https://open.spotify.com/track/2FRnf9qhLbvw8fu4IBXx78) ” by


**[Wham!](https://open.spotify.com/artist/5lpH0xAS4fVfLkACg9DAuM)** , and “


[All I Want For Christmas Is You](https://open.spotify.com/track/0bYg9bo50gSsH3LtXe2SQn) ” by


**[Mariah Carey](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4iHNK0tOyZPYnBU7nGAgpQ)** .


While December is still the main event, for plenty of fans holiday music never gets packed away with the ornaments. In fact, Spotify users created more than 100,000 holiday playlists this September alone—proof that some listeners keep the festive spirit alive all year long.


## **The holiday hits that keep coming back**


When it comes to seasonal staples, fans have their favorites.


[Mariah Carey](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4iHNK0tOyZPYnBU7nGAgpQ) ’s


[ever-popular](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2018-12-18/why-mariah-careys-all-i-want-for-christmas-is-you-is-streamed-more-than-any-other-holiday-song/) “


[All I Want for Christmas Is You](https://open.spotify.com/track/0bYg9bo50gSsH3LtXe2SQn?si=51b67003802042c4) ” remains Spotify’s top-streamed holiday song, while


[Michael Bublé](https://open.spotify.com/artist/1GxkXlMwML1oSg5eLPiAz3) holds the crown as the most popular holiday artist overall.


And plenty more classics are still in rotation. Last December, all five of the top holiday tracks in the U.S. were more than 30 years old, including


“


[Rockin’ Around The Christmas Tree](https://open.spotify.com/track/2EjXfH91m7f8HiJN1yQg97?si=6e5549ca40f84ed3) ” by


[Brenda Lee](https://open.spotify.com/artist/4cPHsZM98sKzmV26wlwD2W) and


[Dean Martin](https://open.spotify.com/artist/49e4v89VmlDcFCMyDv9wQ9) ’s “


[Rudolph, The Red-Nosed Reindeer](https://open.spotify.com/track/2L9QLAhrvtP4EYg1lY0Tnw?si=e17333291f0e4f23) .”


## **The countries where the holiday party starts early**


While listeners in the U.S. may be turning up the holiday tunes in late October, some countries start even earlier. Places like Barbados, Liechtenstein, Denmark, and Iceland are the first to the holiday party, with Barbadian listeners ramping up as early as October 1—a full month before the global average of October 30.


And then there’s the Philippines, a country known for having one of the longest seasonal celebrations. In September, festive listening accounted for 1.3% of total streams, more than double the next-highest market, Colombia. The country has also racked up the most holiday-related searches on Spotify so far this year, followed by the U.S., U.K., Indonesia, and Germany.


## **More holiday surprises are coming soon**


As always, Spotify is the place to find the gifts that keep on giving, including special releases like


[Spotify Singles: Holiday Collection](https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/2025-spotify-singles-holiday-collection/) , where artists put their spin on holiday classics.


At the end of the season, we’ll share the top songs, artists, and albums that defined holiday listening in 2026. Until then, we wish you a very merry (and extra-long) holiday season.
